Q: False alignment rendering in GitHub A:

GitHub only uses MathJax to convert TeX to MathML on the server, so MathJax doesn't actually produce the output in the browser. That is done by the browser's native MathML support. Most browsers implement MathJax-Core, which is a limited version of MathML4 that doesn't include some of the elements and attributes from MathML. MathJax generates MathML3, and uses some elements and attributes that MathML-Core doesn't include.

For example, MathML-Core doesn't include the columnalign attribute that MathJax uses to set the alignment of the columns of your aligned environment. That is, you have <mtable columnalign="right left"...> but MathML-Core ignores the columnalign attribute, so the first column gets the default left alignment.

Some browsers, like Firefox and Safari, implemented MathML before MathML-Core was developed, so they do handle the columnalign attribute, but Chrome and Edge never did, so their MathML-Core version doesn't. That is why you are seeing the misalignment in Chrome, but others are seeing it correctly in Firefox.

If your site actually ran MathJax for the browser-side rendering (rather than using the browsers native MathML rendering), the output would be correct, as MathJax implements MathML3, not MathML-Core. But GitHub doesn't do that, so you get the native rendering instead.

Q: Encryption Iris ODBC 64 Bit A:

You can generate a private key and export the public key as a base64-encoded X.509 certificate and then load the certificate and private key into IRIS as X.509 credentials.

After that create an OAuth2 Server Description using the issuer endpoint and choose the SSL/TLS configuration.

After create an OAuth2 Client Configuration with these settings:

-Application Name: medbank

-Client Type: Confidential

- Required grant types: Client credentials

- Authentication type: private key JWT

- Authentication signing algorithm: RS384

-Audience: https://fhir.epic.com/interconnect-fhir-oauth/oauth2/token

In the JWT Settings tab:

-check Create JWT Settings from X509 credentials

-choose your X509 credentials from the dropdown

-set the signing algorithm for access token algorithms to RS384

And in the Client Credentials tab:

-enter the received Client ID

-if required, enter a client secret value as described in the example. This should help pass X509 Certificate upon calling FHIR API.

Q: how to pass value from one page to another page in oracle apex 5.0? A:

If you do this via a "Redirect to page in this application", then the other form values you have on page 3 will not be POSTed to session state.

There are at least a couple other ways you could accomplish this:

  • You could simply have the Source of item P4_LOT_N be P3_LOT_N.
  • You could define a computation on page 3, to set P4_LOT_N to P3_LOT_N.

Q: Spring Boot - JpaRepository not initializing when using multiple DataSources A:

Why not use Spring Profiles instead of configuring both database connections in a single application.yml file? You can create separate application.yml files for each profile and assign each profile to a different database connection.

By using profiles, you can easily manage different environments (e.g., development, testing, production) with their respective configurations. For example:

Create separate configuration files for each environment:

application-dev.yml for development application-prod.yml for production Activate the profile you need in your main application.yml or as a command-line argument when running your application.

Example: application.yml:

yaml spring: profiles: active: dev application-dev.yml:

yaml spring: datasource: url: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/dev_db username: dev_user password: dev_password application-prod.yml:

yaml spring: datasource: url: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/prod_db username: prod_user password: prod_password This way, you can cleanly separate your database configurations for each profile without cluttering a single file.

Q: DataGridComboBoxColumn binding to ObservableCollection A:

If your platforms are common for all objects, then you can make platforms property static and your xaml will use it as it's shown below:

<DataGridComboBoxColumn
    Header="Role"
    SelectedValueBinding="{Binding Role}"
    ItemsSource="{Binding Source={x:Static local:ProjectsDataContext.Roles}}"
    DisplayMemberPath="Name"/>

Hopefully, it will help.

Q: SharePoint 2010 SecurityTokenService error A:

The solution suggested by Antipod does work when SecurityTokenService is used by your application. However, it doesn't work when it's requested e.g. from Search Application. For example Core Results Search Web Part calls Search Service Application which calls Security Token Service.

In this case SPSecurityContext.SecurityTokenForContext method is called and it requests SecurityTokenService. In this case binding timeouts are not applied because SecurityTokenService WCF binding is initialized in following way:

s_CachedActAsStsBinding = new CustomBinding(bindingElementsInTopDownChannelStackOrder);

where bindingElementsInTopDownChannelStackOrder are taken from configuration in 14\WebClients folder but timeout parameters are not applied.

You can try solutions suggested here: http://www.eventid.net/display.asp?eventid=8306&eventno=10757&source=Microsoft-SharePoint%20Products-SharePoint%20Foundatio&phase=1 but unfortunately they didn't work for me.

Q: Create selectizeInput() with labels from an existing table A:

You're close, I think. Though, as @lailaps suggests, we really could do with more information.

This may give you what you want. The key is to format your correspondence table the way selectizeInput expects its choices to be formatted.

library(shiny)

# Correspondence table
choices <- tibble::tibble(
  choice = list("Choice 1" = c("1A","1B"),"Choice 2" = c("2A","2B"))
)


ui <- fluidPage(
  selectizeInput( 
    "select", 
    "Select options below:", 
    choices = choices$choice
  ),
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {}

shinyApp(ui, server)

If you need to modify the choices once the app has initialised, updateSelectizeInput is the way to go.

Q: How to add flags or marks to tcp net.connect() for later ip rule based routing A:

node's net api doesn't expose SO_MARK (the socket option that actually sets an fwmark), so there's no clean way to mark per-connection from net.connect() without a native addon. but you don't really need marks here.

you already have working src-based routing. the only thing missing is a distinct source per target, so give each one its own local source address and bind to it. add a couple of alias ips on the host:

ip addr add 10.10.0.1/32 dev lo
ip addr add 10.10.0.2/32 dev lo

then bind per target in node:

net.connect({ host: '192.168.155.5', port, localAddress: '10.10.0.1' }) // target1
net.connect({ host: '192.168.155.5', port, localAddress: '10.10.0.2' }) // target2

and route by source exactly like you do now:

ip rule add from 10.10.0.1 table 101
ip rule add from 10.10.0.2 table 102

since the endpoints all share 192.168.155.5 you can't tell them apart by destination, and the source port is ephemeral, so the local source address is the one knob you control at connect() time. this reuses the src-based routing that already works instead of adding fwmark plumbing.

if you specifically need fwmark for other reasons, that's SO_MARK via setsockopt, which means an N-API addon (or running separate processes and marking by uid with ip rule add uidrange). the localAddress route avoids all of that.

Q: Extract file basename without path and extension in bash A:

Use pure Bash, without any basename, and without any variable juggling. Set a string and echo:

p=/the/path/foo.txt
echo "${p//+(*\/|.*)}"

Output:

foo

Note: The Bash extglob option must be "on", (Ubuntu sets extglob "on" by default). If it's not, do:

shopt -s extglob

Walking through the ${p//+(*\/|.*)}:

  1. ${p -- start with $p.
  2. // substitute every instance of the pattern that follows.
  3. +( match one or more of the pattern list in parenthesis, (i.e. until item #7 below).
  4. 1st pattern: *\/ matches anything before a literal "/" char.
  5. pattern separator | which in this instance acts like a logical OR.
  6. 2nd pattern: .* matches anything after a literal "." -- that is, in bash the "." is just a period char, and not a regex dot.
  7. ) end pattern list.
  8. } end parameter expansion. With a string substitution, there's usually another / there, followed by a replacement string. But since there isn't any / there, the matched patterns are substituted with nothing; this deletes the matches.

Relevant man bash background:

  1. pattern substitution:

    ${parameter/pattern/string}
        Pattern substitution.  The pattern is expanded to produce a pat
        tern just as in pathname expansion.  Parameter is  expanded  and
        the  longest match of pattern against its value is replaced with
        string.  If pattern begins with /, all matches  of  pattern  are
        replaced   with  string.   Normally  only  the  first  match  is
        replaced.  If pattern begins with #, it must match at the begin‐
        ning of the expanded value of parameter.  If pattern begins with
        %, it must match at the end of the expanded value of  parameter.
        If string is null, matches of pattern are deleted and the / fol
        lowing pattern may be omitted.  If parameter is @ or *, the sub
        stitution  operation  is applied to each positional parameter in
        turn, and the expansion is the resultant list.  If parameter  is
        an  array  variable  subscripted  with  @ or *, the substitution
        operation is applied to each member of the array  in  turn,  and
        the expansion is the resultant list.

  2. extended pattern matching:

    If the extglob shell option is enabled using the shopt builtin, several
extended  pattern  matching operators are recognized.  In the following
description, a pattern-list is a list of one or more patterns separated
by a |.  Composite patterns may be formed using one or more of the fol
lowing sub-patterns:

       ?(pattern-list)
              Matches zero or one occurrence of the given patterns
       *(pattern-list)
              Matches zero or more occurrences of the given patterns
       +(pattern-list)
              Matches one or more occurrences of the given patterns
       @(pattern-list)
              Matches one of the given patterns
       !(pattern-list)
              Matches anything except one of the given patterns
